grh_d26123b8a7b4e23b27e3.title: The Choosing
paragraphs: After an emergency landing in an authoritarian African country, six Americans are imprisoned by dictator Mandu Rana. They are first told all will be executed, then informed that only one must die and that they themselves must choose the victim. Rejecting a random drawing, they hold a grim trial in which each person argues for the value of his or her life. The group discovers that wealthy Franklin P. Butler is an arms dealer who has supplied weapons to conflicts like the one around them. Elderly Mr. Rosen volunteers to die, but Butler tries to buy both Rosen and the others. When the final vote ties between Rosen and Butler, Elizabeth chooses Butler, who is taken away for execution. Rosen then dies naturally, leaving the survivors to face the bitter irony that Butler may be shot with weapons he helped sell.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes [[person|dane-clark|Dane Clark]], Hans Conried, Mary Jane Croft, and [[person|parley-baer|Parley Baer]]. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Steve Sharon as writer, and Richard Widmark as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_d21f07b13ddc4d7e23db.title: Blue Bride
paragraphs: Operating from Bordeaux, Harry arranges a large counterfeit-currency deal while rival Baras closes in on him. To distract the opposition, Harry cultivates Baras's bride Sofia, while the endlessly helpful Professor Saint-Pierre keeps blundering into the scheme. Harry eventually flees with a suitcase full of bogus notes and is nearly stopped by police; Saint-Pierre's innocent testimony briefly convinces them Harry is only an eccentric scholar. Moments later an old man finds the spilled suitcase and displays the counterfeit money, sending Harry running from Bordeaux with the police siren behind him.
